newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE nearby canola ends down on commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE nearby canola ends down on commercial selling.

text.p: WCE nearby canola ended down on commercial selling as crushers bought deferred months, traders said.

"Saskatchewan Wheat Pool was a heavy seller at the close, funds sold 500 July, crushers bought November," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -0.76 Thursday from -2.35 Wednesday. July-Nov spread at $29, Aug-Nov $28.50, July Aug $1. Volume was 5,650 lots, or 113,000 tonnes, 324 hedges.
Japan bought 5,000-6,000 tonnes of canola overnight, sources said.

July canola closed $0.90 lower at $408.10 and November finished up $0.40 at $381.90. July flax closed up $1.40 at $332.50, met by light hedges and September settled up $0.90 at $323.40. UGG sold 100 Sep-Nov at $1, traders said.
July western barley rose $0.50 to $136.50 as Alberta Wheat Pool bought and October was unchanged at $136.50 with PCTS buying, 200 July-Oct at even money. Oats did not trade.
Expectations the Canadian Wheat Board will increase its world barley price outlook in Thursday May Pool Return Outlook at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT buoyed nearby WCE barley, traders said.
Alberta Wheat Pool bought July feed wheat up $1 to $160, floor sources said. Volume was 625 lots. Mar-May spread at $2.
PCTS sold 25 October feed pea contracts unchanged at US$187.50, a trader said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
